title: Investigation Workbench Runbook and Signal Experiment Canvas
content:
Purpose:
This is an operational-first playbook intended to unify how engineers run investigations against LLM inference incidents and experimental signal changes. It pairs a lightweight runbook (investigation workbench) with an experiment canvas for short A/B-style telemetry adjustments (probe coverage, trace enrichment, dashboard widgets). The goal: reduce time-to-root-cause for token-serving and routing issues while keeping trace/query costs bounded.

Scope and audience:
- Audience: oncall SREs, serving engineers, ML infra, and product leads running rollouts.
- Scope: production inference paths (hosted + dedicated) — cold cache, routing fallbacks, throughput throttles, model-fallbacks, and correctness regressions tied to prompts. Not a replacement for postmortems; this is the immediate triage + experiment instrument.

High-level goals (what success looks like):
- Investigations that reach a working hypothesis in <45 minutes for 80% of latency anomalies.
- Standardized signal kit (3–6 probes) that covers 90% of common root causes (cold cache, batching congestion, KV cache misses, model overload, tenant throttling).
- Prototype tracing enrichment experiments that can be run with a single feature-flagged rollout and rolled back automatically after 24–72 hours.

Quick glossary (avoid ambiguity):
- Probe: a synthetic or passive metric/trace instrument introduced to verify a specific hypothesis (e.g., per-route embed-cache-hit-rate).
- Workbench: a lightweight set of dashboards, trace filters, and CLI snippets for a single investigation.
- Signal experiment: a short-lived telemetry change (higher sampling, new tag, new probe metric) with clear rollback criteria.

Investigation Workbench runbook (stepwise):
1) Intake and triage (0–10m):
   - Ingest alert: identify primary SLI breached (p50/p95 latency, error-rate, token-cost surge).
   - Capture initial context: example request id(s), model, route, tenant, region, commit/version (if available).
   - Quick sanity checks: infra capacity dashboards, model queue length, autoscaler events.

2) Narrow to hypothesis (10–25m):
   - Use sessionized trace timeline (session id anchored) to find where latency accumulation occurs: pre-processing, tokenization, routing, KV warmup, model forward pass, postprocessing.
   - If traces are sparse, immediately launch a signal experiment: bump trace-sampling for the affected route to 100% for 10 minutes OR enable sample-by-tenant for the tenant AND tag requests with `investigation_id=<id>`.
   - Check probe coverage checklist (see below) and enable any missing probes as feature flags.

3) Confirm & isolate (25–45m):
   - Validate hypothesis by changing one variable: toggle cache warm policies, switch model variant to a lower-latency quantized variant, disable batching for a short window, or reroute traffic to another region.
   - Use differential queries: compare percentiles for affected vs control tenants, or pre/post toggle windows.

4) Mitigation & communication (45–90m):
   - Apply a short-lived mitigation (traffic steering or weight rollback) if evidence indicates immediate user impact.
   - Post a status update with hypothesis, mitigation, and next steps in the incident channel.

5) Post-investigation (same day):
   - If telemetry experiment ran, capture artifact links and revert sampling/flags automatically via the rollback play.
   - If mitigation still needed, open a ticket with owners and required actions.

Signal experiment canvas (template):
- Title: short name.
- Owner: person oncall/engineer.
- Hypothesis: single-sentence testable claim (e.g., "Increasing route trace sampling will show that KV cache misses cause P95 spikes").
- Probe(s) to enable: list (e.g., route-kv-cache-hit, batch-queue-depth, model-latency-by-size).
- Sampling change: from baseline -> experiment (%), duration, scope (route/tenant/all).
- Dashboard widgets to compare: control vs experiment (p50/p95, token-rate, cache-hit-rate).
- Success criteria: quantitative threshold that confirms hypothesis.
- Rollback criteria: query-cost > X or no evidence in 24h.

Probe coverage checklist (prioritized, minimal set):
- Ingress rate + small-window surge probe (1m granularity)
- Per-route KV cache hit ratio (per-tenant)
- Batch queue length / max waiting time
- Model-side concurrency and queue depth
- Tokenization time (client-side vs server-side split)
- Model variant fallback count (routing fallbacks)
- Tenant throttles and 429 counts

Metric definitions (short canonical forms to avoid drift):
- p95-inference-latency: 95th percentile time from request accepted to first token emitted (ms).
- kv-cache-hit-rate: fraction of requests where prefix/KV cached context satisfied initial KV lookup.
- batch-wait-ms: median queue wait time for batching bucket in ms.
- model-forward-ms: model compute time excluding queue/warmup (measured at worker boundary).
- tenant-429-rate: 429 responses per 1k requests (normalized per tenant).

Tracing guidance & minimal span contract (for experiments):
- Core spans: client->ingress, ingress->router, router->batcher, batcher->worker, worker->model_forward, model_forward->response_builder, response_builder->send.
- Required span annotations: tenant_id, route, model_name, model_variant, seq_length, batch_size, kv_cache_hit (true/false), investigation_id (when active).
- Sampling heuristic for experiments: sample by investigation_id override (keeps tracetagged sequences) or route-based dynamic sampling to cap trace volume at N/day.
- Sensitive fields: do not record prompt plaintext in spans; use prompt_hash and store prompt snippets only in ephemeral, access-audited stores.

Dashboard mapping (what to add to a workbench):
- Top panel: p50/p95 latency overlay (affected route vs platform baseline).
- Probe panel: KV cache hit rate by tenant (rollup + per-tenant links).
- Batch panel: batch queue depth heatmap and batch-size distribution.
- Model panel: worker CPU/GPU busy, model-forward-ms histogram, model-queue-depth.
- Error panel: 5xx/4xx/429 by tenant and by route.
- Trace links: quick filter to show traces with investigation_id and kv_cache_hit=false.

Example vignette (cold-cache spike):
- Symptom: P95 spike at 15:12 UTC, single region, affecting 3 tenants.
- Quick triage: ingress rate normal; batch queue growth observed; kv-cache-hit-rate dipped to 10% for affected tenants.
- Experiment: enable route trace-sampling 100% for 5m and tag with investigation_id=20251120-cache-spike; enable a temporary probe to count cold-start worker initializations.
- Finding: traces show worker process-initialization and model warmup dominating the 95th percentile; pipeline showing many small batches with seq_length variance causing poor packing.
- Mitigation: increase burst capacity for region and enable a short-term batching window adjustment; followup ticket to pre-warm workers for high-risk tenants.

Operational safety and cost guardrails:
- Any sampling increase must have an automated throttle: cost-budget per investigation (default $50/day) and auto-roll back after budget or time limit.
- Probes that roll up high-cardinality tags (e.g., prompt_hash, tenant+route+user-id) require approval and TTL of 72 hours.

Open questions & TODOs:
- How to standardize per-tenant sampling caps across Dedicated vs Hosted? (ACTION: define default caps and escalation path)
- Small experiment to test capture of model variant telemetry without adding cardinality — proposal due EOW. (OWNER: Marta)
- Integration checklist for embedding sampled traces into Confluence incident artifacts automatically.

Immediate next steps:
- Share this workbench template with oncall rotation and run a tabletop using last month’s cold-cache incident. (Owner: Asha)
- Implement automated rollback for sampling flags in feature-flag service (low priority: queue up in infra sprint).
- Add a "one-click" dashboard sandbox link in the Incident Slack flow.

Notes to self: this doc is intentionally lightweight — prefer concrete probes and a single-variable-change approach. Keep the experiment canvas short and require numerical success/rollback criteria.

References:
- Incident examples: JIRA-INC-2025-091 (cold-cache), JIRA-INC-2025-142 (routing fallback).
- Related playbooks: observability/operator-playlist-routing-eviction-dashboard-onboarding (see shared drive)

-- end of doc --
